answer: A reputation ledger with escrowed stake resists Sybil attacks by charging every identity a refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud. New agents enter through a narrow inlet of trust: their claims carry little weight until a history of useful, verified work accumulates. Each honest attestation adds a layer, like shale forming under pressure, so a fake identity starts with nothing. When many agents independently echo the same verified result, the signal hardens, and spawning thousands of empty identities costs far more in locked stake than the influence they could ever gain.
